impact_assessment.mitigation: Deterministic placement, 24-seed availability coverage, focused shop-line tests and a browser check on a fresh server; the map is refreshed after the change.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Content expansion: six new enemy records (Bone Picker, Lantern Wraith, Cinder Stalker, Spire Marksman, Reliquary Warden, Salt Orchard Hydra) using tinted borrowed sheets with boss-scale frames and patterns; two new late sections, The Gilded Reliquary (section 22) and The Salt Orchard (section 23), pushing the Keeper to 24 and the First Memory finale to 25; new mobs added to four existing rosters. Quest expansion: a second chapter for every resident (12 quests), chapter-aware selection, an epilogue per chapter, late story lines, and a persisted tracked-quest with a HUD tracker. Tests: content-expansion and quest-chapters plus intentional updates to section-count, checkpoint, depth-clamp and quest-reference assertions (ADR-226).

impact_assessment.why: Player request for new enemies, new sections, a better quest log, and better quests and story.
impact_assessment.benefits: Two more late road stops with new guardians and mobs, discoverable late enemies across four existing biomes, six new quest chapters with closing story beats, and a pinned quest line that follows the run.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: FINAL_DEPTH moves 22 to 24, Meta gains trackedQuest, quest selection becomes chapter-aware; dependency: borrowed sheets must exist in the atlas for every new enemy; concurrency: none; state: old saves at depth 22 now load The Salt Orchard, and old meta defaults trackedQuest null.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Plans are depth-sequential and covered by a new expansion test, atlas ids are reused keys, defaults cover old saves, and the migration change is named in ADR-226.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Add a Bestiary tab to the Memories codex: every one of the 97 enemy records is listed with regular enemies before guardians, a first kill stores the def id in Meta.bestiary and announces itself, and a recorded species reveals its field-guide line while unknown ones stay sealed. bestiaryEntries sorts and filters phantom saved ids; memoriesScreen takes the saved record and switches panels through Memories/Bestiary tabs. impact_assessment.why: The Memories screen only showed lore, so the 97 defeated species had no codex and a first kill said nothing about the record it created.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can see what they have met, guardians are separated from mobs, unknown entries tease the deep, and the first kill is announced and persisted.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Meta gains bestiary (defaults []); dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: old saves default the empty record; UI: the Memories screen gains a second panel and tab row.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Schema default plus phantom-id filtering, a 5-case suite, source/CSS wiring assertions, and browser checks at desktop and phone widths before the UI task closes.
